title: I’m still new to making mods and games with AI, but one tip has already saved me a lot of frustration:
author: Golfballtaucher12
selftext: Before you start, let the AI build the tools it needs to work more effectively. Giving it time to create its own debugging and development tools can save you a lot of frustration later on.

comments.author: 2nd_breakfastt
comments.body:
Yes good idea. Can you provide more info on how you have the ai build the tools and how they then apply to your project? 

I have a similar development process and want to compare

replies.author: Golfballtaucher12
replies.body:
I’m making a mod for a game that allows characters to perform idle animations (reading, eating, etc.), but the animations kept failing or behaving incorrectly.  
At first, the AI simply couldn’t figure out why. After literally hours of trying to get things working, every new "patch" made things worse and the code increasingly messy. I was getting so frustrated that I was close to deleting the entire mod.  
Then my Idea was: why not let the AI create a diagnostic tool to help identify the problem? it created a tool specifically designed to detect animation-related issues in the mod. (it was the Idea of the AI to search there for the problem) AI is really good in knowing where the problem can be, but not how to fix it, but with a tool it perfectly can point to the problem.)  
Literally 20 seconds after running the tool in-game, the AI found the problem.  
This is exactly why tools like these are so valuable and necessary. Even studios that don't use AI face similar challenges and rely on debugging tools, diagnostic software, and other solutions to identify and fix problems.

replies.author: 2nd_breakfastt
replies.body: Awesome. Great use of AI to problem solve and be efficient. I’ll definitely look to add in similar tactics thanks

replies.author: No-Tradition-6039
replies.body: But how do u teach the ai? Like u created a skill inside claude?

comments.author: Restnrelax
comments.body: Yeah. I had it make a “workshop” tool so I can edit or replace individual text, audio, textures, and animations myself if needed, I also had it build in a character editor and builder for making NPCs.

replies.author: Golfballtaucher12
replies.body: Not gone, Lie. I didn't think about tools like that, but it makes sense. Letting the AI create a "workshop" for you, and then crafting it yourself. Thanks, I'm going to make that too.
